rationale:
`src/execution_coverage/check.rs#fn[check_in]` is a site. It is a repository-validation function that collects messages in a local named `errors`. I judged each early exit and found no gap.

- `workspace_root(project)?` is the first statement. No check has run before it, and every later check needs the root, so nothing independent is skipped.
- `exceptions(&root, &outlines, &mut errors)?` is the second `?`. In `fn[exceptions]`, the only failure that can occur, a definitions load failure, is pushed to `errors`. It then returns `Ok(BTreeMap::new())`, so the function never returns `Err`. Later checks still run.
- `path.strip_prefix(&root).map_err(io::Error::other)?` cannot fail for paths discovered under `root`. It is a conversion, not a check.
- The `continue` after a parse error from `outlines.parse` and the `continue` after an `inventory` error only skip work that needs that file's parse or inventory. The error is recorded first, and the loop moves on to other files.
- The `continue` under `if !measured` skips the per-file threshold and function checks. They depend on the measurement data, and a measurement failure is already in `errors`. The in-code comment says no exception can clear it. Parsing and inventory checks run before this `continue`, so they are independent of measurement and are not skipped.
- The `continue` inside `for function in functions` is a success path, taken when a function was executed. It skips only the error reporting for that function.

The per-record checks (stale, unreadable, function attribution, corrupt attribution) are separate `if` statements with no early exit. All of them run in the same loop iteration. The final `errors.retain(|error| seen.insert(error.clone()))` removes duplicate messages, so one failure is not reported twice. The function finishes by listing every collected error in one report.

text: Repository validation MUST continue after a failed check and report every failed
check it finds in one run, each as a {term}`requirements.ci.validation_error`.
This is a convention for every validation error; the requirement for each check
states which conditions that check reports. A file that cannot be parsed, such as
a malformed `habeas.toml`, `book.toml`, or evidence file, is one failed check:
its error MAY report only the first parse or decoding problem in that file, and
checks that do not depend on its contents MUST still run.
The code that sequences the repository's checks carries out the first paragraph.
A repository-validation function that collects validation errors MUST hold them
in a parameter or local variable named `errors`, and a function with such a
variable is a site below; authoring code that collects errors only to abort is
not one. After one of its checks fails, a site MUST still run every later check
that does not depend on the failed check's result, including later checks in the
same loop iteration, and MUST NOT report one failure twice.
One message in a repository validation report, describing a single failed check.
